text: {"question":"How does the inclusion of high‑redshift data and local distance ladder measurements jointly influence the statistical preference for extended dark‑energy models compared to the ΛCDM baseline, and what role does the additional parameter penalty play in this assessment?","reference_answer":"When high‑redshift observations such as CMB distance priors are added, the extended models PEDE and GDE lose their advantage because their extra parameters do not sufficiently improve the fit, whereas GEDE remains competitive due to a smaller penalty. Conversely, excluding local SH0ES data removes the ability of these models to raise H₀, so Bayesian evidence and AIC/DIC no longer favor them over ΛCDM. Thus, both datasets together demonstrate that model complexity must be justified by a significant likelihood gain to overcome the information‑criterion penalties.","passage_1_contribution":"High‑redshift CMB data penalize extended models with extra parameters, leaving GEDE as the most competitive extension.","passage_2_contribution":"Local SH0ES measurements are essential for extended models to achieve higher H₀ values; without them, the models do not outperform ΛCDM.","joint_reason":"Both passages show that the statistical preference for extended models depends on the specific observational data included, and that the penalty for additional parameters can outweigh any fit improvement unless the data (high‑redshift or local H₀) strongly support the extension.","same_quantity":false}
